title: Choose the visual world for the Fresh Fingers landing page
question: The roll assigned The Photobooth Strip. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Photobooth Strip
options.lineage: Coin-op photobooths at stations, clubs and arcades: the curtain, the 3-2-1 countdown, the flash, the strip of four frames dropping into the tray
options.thesis: The page is a photobooth: the moment before the flash is the Fresh Fingers moment, and the strip of four frames is the four brands.
options.viewport: Full-bleed dark booth interior; huge caps FRESH WHEN YOU NEED IT. with an italic 'ready?' countdown 3·2·1; a white flash reveals the four-frame strip sliding in from the top, each frame lit in one brand's colour (Fresh Fingers royal blue, CleanGo red, FreshMate deep blue, Finger Fresh lime/pink) with that pack floating inside; primary action 'Pobierz deck' printed on the strip's tail, 'Kontakt' beside it.
options.risk: Playful booth metaphor can read consumer-only; the business close must land as crisply as the flash, or investors see a toy.

raised.raise: The intro pours in line by line like a title screen: the countdown and headline arrive as a timed sequence, not a fade.
The strip is one rail with a fixed frame pitch: scrolling scrubs with inertia and always settles on a whole frame, never between brands.
One master timeline drives every motion on the page (curtain, flash, strip, pack float); nothing animates on its own clock.
One cool white edge marks the active frame; every other frame stays in its own colour at rest.

options.label: Lit by the Moment
options.lineage: Nightclub lighting rigs: gel washes, moving heads, haze, the room re-lit in one colour per track
options.thesis: The whole page is a stage wash that re-lights per brand: four gels, four colours, the packs floating under moving light.
options.viewport: Black room, a single beam sweeps to reveal FRESH WHEN YOU NEED IT. in huge caps with an italic line beneath; the Fresh Fingers pack floats centre under blue light; scrolling swings the rig to red, deep blue and lime as each sibling brand takes the floor; 'Pobierz deck' as a lit sign bottom-right.
options.risk: Dark ground plus coloured light is the nightlife look most runs in this category land on; it wins on atmosphere and loses on surprise.

options.label: Night-Market Sign River
options.lineage: Night-market streets: lantern colour, awnings, steam, hand-painted stall boards
options.thesis: Four brands as four stalls on one night street, each sign its own voice, one river of light leading to the business stall at the end.
options.viewport: A street receding into the page, four lit stalls in brand colours, headline hand-painted across the first awning, packs on the counters; the deck and contact wait at the last stall.
options.case: Holds audience identification (night, city, meeting people) but loses product clarity: hand-painted chaos fights the three-second brand hierarchy.
options.risk: Becomes a scene rather than a page if the stalls are not strict columns.

options.label: ANSI BBS Nightboard
options.lineage: 2 a.m. dial-up bulletin boards, sixteen ANSI colours on black
options.thesis: The brand as a text screen that pours in at modem speed.
options.viewport: Centered title art over numbered menu lines.
options.risk: Text-only chrome cannot show the packs.
options.case: Loses both axes: partners and investors do not identify with textmode, and a character grid hides the product.
options.kept: Line-by-line timed arrival for the intro.

options.label: Cutting Bench Select Rail
options.lineage: Film editor's bench: perforated rail, punched frames, tape flags
options.thesis: Sections as frames on one perforated rail.
options.viewport: One orange rail across the sheet, frames strung along it.
options.risk: One-ink orange erases four brand colours.
options.case: Loses both axes: an editor's tool is not the audience's world, and a single ink cannot carry four colour worlds.
options.kept: Fixed frame pitch: scrolling snaps to whole frames with inertia.

options.label: Pulp Rocketship Plate
options.thesis: Freshness on the go as a finned rocket on a diagonal.
options.viewport: A pack crossing the page on a diagonal with speed lines.
options.case: Loses both axes: nostalgia is not this audience, and pulp paper contradicts the premium-modern commitment.
options.kept: Motion as a committed diagonal trajectory, not a hover.

options.label: Moon-Shadow Bazaar
options.lineage: A surreal night bazaar trading in shadows
options.thesis: Moments as tradable shadows down one moonlit lane.
options.viewport: Stalls ranked down one lane, each item ticketed.
options.case: Loses both axes: too abstract for partners, and shadows hide the pack.
options.kept: One cool white edge marks the active item.

options.label: Paper Automata Menagerie
options.thesis: Four brands as figures on one crank.
options.viewport: A procession of figures over one crank line.
options.case: Loses both axes: kraft and cut paper read handmade, not nightlife-premium, and a menagerie obscures the product.
options.kept: One master timeline drives every motion.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The DTC oral-care page: white ground, pack hero, benefit icons, brand grid, contact strip; executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline left, pack right, four brand tiles below, benefits row, download deck and contact at the end.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every oral-care brand by design.
